Key Observations

🎯 Risk-Adjusted Returns

The RL portfolio has a Sharpe ratio of 1.46 (above the benchmark's 1.45) and a Sortino ratio of 2.13 on a single out-of-sample period. One period and one training seed are not enough to claim a durable edge.

📊 Market Exposure

With a Beta of 0.88, the portfolio moved roughly 88% as much as the market, at 11.3% annualized volatility. The 10% position cap and 50-asset universe bound concentration.

⚡ Transaction Cost Impact

Average daily turnover was 1.1% of the portfolio at a 0.25% cost per unit of turnover. Costs are deducted from every simulated return.

🔄 Moody-Saffell Differential Sharpe

The online differential Sharpe ratio reward (Moody & Saffell, 1998) provides a temporally smooth learning signal via exponential moving averages. This avoids the noisy per-step return signals that destabilize RL training, enabling stable convergence with bounded rewards.

🏗️ LSTM Temporal Modeling

The 2-layer LSTM with 128 hidden units processes 60-day lookback windows of 5 features per asset (log returns, volatility, RSI, MACD, Bollinger %B), and feeds the encoded history to the actor and critic heads.

📈 Alpha

Measured alpha is positive at 0.86% annualized versus the S&P 500. No significance test was run, so a value this close to zero should not be read as evidence of skill.

⚠️ Concentration Constraints

The 10% max position size and long-only constraints limit how far the agent can overweight any single name. This is a deliberate risk-management choice that can cost return in concentrated rallies.

🎲 Gaussian Policy with Softmax

Rather than Dirichlet distributions (which lack MPS support), the actor uses Gaussian distributions in unconstrained logit space followed by softmax normalization. This MPS-compatible approach produces valid portfolio weight simplices while enabling efficient GPU-accelerated training on Apple Silicon.
